meta.name: Fastener Engineering Atlas
meta.warning: Not a substitute for purchased standards, design codes, MTCs or engineering approval.
meta.thread_database_version: V2.2 expanded: metric ISO selected coarse/fine, Unified UNC/UNF/UNEF common sizes, plus existing pipe/power threads

meta.description: Expanded engineering reference database with detailed standards, materials, fasteners, threads, coating procedures, compatibility records and engineering warnings.
meta.database_expansion: Expanded baseline corresponding to the planned v1.2 database scope; release number intentionally reset to v1.0.0 for the new repository.

standards.title: Hexagon head bolts, partial thread
standards.scope: Hexagon head bolts with partially threaded shank in the legacy DIN metric product family. It is primarily a dimensional/product-design reference for head geometry, shank/thread configuration and nominal dimensions; mechanical strength is assigned separately by the applicable material/property specification.
standards.engineering_use: Covers metric hexagon-head bolts with a threaded portion shorter than the nominal shank length. Commonly encountered on legacy drawings and equipment; for new procurement, verify the applicable DIN EN ISO replacement and exact dimensions.

standards.title: Hexagon head screws, full thread
standards.scope: Legacy DIN product standard for fully threaded hexagon-head screws. It defines the product form and dimensional family rather than the material strength class.
standards.engineering_use: Used for fully threaded metric hex-head fasteners. Confirm the current DIN EN ISO product standard, tolerance and property class before substitution.

standards.title: Hexagon nuts
standards.scope: Legacy DIN dimensional standard for regular hexagon nuts. It defines the nut geometry and dimensional series; nut mechanical performance comes from the applicable property-class/material specification.
standards.engineering_use: Common legacy metric hex-nut reference. Current procurement should identify the applicable ISO/DIN EN ISO nut product and property class.

standards.title: Hexagon socket head cap screws
standards.scope: Legacy DIN standard for hexagon socket head cap screws. It establishes the product geometry and dimensions for socket-head screws.
standards.engineering_use: Used widely on machinery and general mechanical assemblies; ISO 4762 is the corresponding modern international product reference.

standards.title: Plain washers
standards.scope: Legacy DIN family for plain flat washers. It addresses washer geometry and dimensional series rather than bolt material strength.
standards.engineering_use: Used to distribute bearing load beneath bolt heads or nuts and to protect joint surfaces. Verify the exact washer series and hardness requirement for structural or high-load joints.

standards.title: Spring lock washers
standards.scope: Legacy DIN family for split spring lock washers. It defines the washer geometry historically used as a locking element.
standards.engineering_use: Often found on legacy machinery, but its suitability as a locking method must be assessed for the actual joint; do not assume a split washer prevents loosening in every vibration application.

standards.title: Prevailing torque hexagon nuts with non-metallic insert
standards.scope: Legacy DIN product standard for prevailing-torque hexagon nuts using a non-metallic insert. It defines the nut form and locking feature.
standards.engineering_use: Suitable where the temperature, chemical environment and reuse requirements are compatible with the insert material. Check the current replacement standard and prevailing-torque requirements.

standards.title: All-metal prevailing torque hexagon nuts
standards.scope: Legacy DIN product standard for all-metal prevailing-torque hexagon nuts. It defines the locking nut geometry and prevailing-torque feature.
standards.engineering_use: Useful where a polymer insert is unsuitable, especially at elevated temperature. Actual prevailing torque and reuse requirements must be verified against the current specification.

standards.title: Hexagon flange screws
standards.scope: DIN product family for hexagon flange screws, combining a hexagon head with an integral flange for load distribution.
standards.engineering_use: Used where the integrated flange reduces local bearing pressure and can simplify assembly. Confirm flange diameter, head dimensions, thread length and applicable property class.

standards.title: Hexagon flange nuts
standards.scope: DIN product family for hexagon flange nuts with an integral bearing flange.
standards.engineering_use: Used to distribute nut bearing load and can reduce the need for a separate washer. The flange does not by itself define mechanical strength or suitability for structural joints.

standards.title: Lifting eye bolts
standards.scope: DIN standard for lifting eye bolts intended for lifting applications. It addresses geometry, marking and lifting-related requirements rather than ordinary bolting service.
standards.engineering_use: Must be treated as lifting hardware, not as a generic high-strength bolt. Lifting configuration, loading direction, installation and rated capacity require specific verification.

standards.title: Lifting eye nuts
standards.scope: DIN standard for lifting eye nuts. It defines the lifting-eye form and associated requirements for lifting applications.
standards.engineering_use: Use only within the intended lifting configuration and rated capacity. Do not substitute ordinary nuts based only on nominal thread size.

standards.title: Studs, metal end approximately 1.25d
standards.scope: Current DIN standard for studs with a defined metal-end/thread arrangement, including approximately 1.25d engagement at the metal end. It establishes stud dimensions and applicable metric thread combinations.
standards.engineering_use: Used for screwed stud connections where the stud is installed into a tapped component and a nut is fitted on the free end. Material and property class are specified separately.

standards.title: Designation of bolts, screws, studs and nuts
standards.scope: DIN designation system for bolts, screws, studs and nuts. It provides rules for how fastener types, dimensions and finishes are designated so that a drawing or specification can identify a product consistently.
standards.engineering_use: Useful for interpreting legacy DIN callouts and translating them into modern product terminology. It is a designation reference, not a mechanical-property standard.

standards.title: Reduced-shank bolted connections — application/survey
standards.scope: DIN standard for reduced-shank bolted connections, giving the application, survey and examples for high-performance bolted joints. It addresses the joint concept and geometry used to obtain controlled elastic behaviour and high fatigue resistance.
standards.engineering_use: Particularly relevant to pressure equipment, power generation and other highly loaded joints where reduced-shank studs are selected as a system. Calculation and installation requirements must be taken from the applicable edition and companion parts.

standards.title: Reduced-shank bolted connections — studs
standards.scope: DIN component standard within the reduced-shank bolting system, focused on studs. It defines the stud configuration used with reduced-shank bolted connections.
standards.engineering_use: Use together with the relevant DIN 2510 system requirements; do not treat the stud dimensions as a standalone allowable-stress specification.

standards.title: Special mechanical properties for fasteners at low/high temperature
standards.scope: DIN technical supply standard covering special mechanical properties for fasteners intended for service at low and high temperatures, including the temperature range identified by the standard.
standards.engineering_use: Relevant when ordinary room-temperature property classes are insufficient. Exact temperature-dependent properties and manufacturing requirements must be checked in the current edition.

standards.title: Mechanical properties — bolts, screws and studs
standards.scope: ISO standard specifying mechanical and physical properties for carbon/alloy-steel bolts, screws and studs with specified property classes. It applies to ISO metric coarse and fine-pitch threads within the stated diameter ranges and evaluates properties at 10–35 °C.
standards.engineering_use: It defines property-class requirements such as tensile strength, proof/yield-related requirements and hardness, but it does not establish design allowable stress, fatigue resistance, corrosion resistance or torque/clamp-force performance. The 2013 edition remains current after a 2025 review while a replacement is under development.

standards.title: Mechanical properties — nuts
standards.scope: ISO standard for mechanical and physical properties of nuts made from carbon steel or alloy steel and assigned property classes. It establishes requirements for nut performance and matching with bolt property classes.
standards.engineering_use: Use with ISO 898-1 when selecting metric steel nuts. It is a property standard, not the dimensional product standard for every nut shape.

standards.title: Stainless steel bolts, screws and studs
standards.scope: ISO property standard for corrosion-resistant stainless-steel bolts, screws and studs. It establishes designation and mechanical-property classes for austenitic, martensitic, ferritic and duplex stainless fasteners.
standards.engineering_use: Important for stainless selection because property class and material family are linked. The standard cautions that selection outside the normal reference temperature range requires additional engineering consideration; high-temperature service is addressed by the ISO 3506 series.

standards.title: Stainless steel nuts
standards.scope: ISO property standard for corrosion-resistant stainless-steel nuts. It defines material/property designations and mechanical requirements for matching stainless fastener systems.
standards.engineering_use: Use with ISO 3506-1 bolt/screw/stud classes and the applicable nut product dimensions.

standards.title: Stainless steel set screws
standards.scope: ISO property standard for stainless-steel set screws and similar threaded fasteners with specified hardness/property classes.
standards.engineering_use: Applies to small threaded retaining fasteners where tensile bolt property-class rules are not appropriate. Check the exact product geometry and hardness class.

standards.title: Special stainless/nickel-alloy fasteners for high temperature
standards.scope: ISO standard addressing special stainless-steel and nickel-alloy fasteners for applications at elevated temperature. It supplements the ordinary stainless fastener property framework where temperature changes the required material selection and properties.
standards.engineering_use: Use when service temperature is beyond the normal range for ISO 3506-1 selection. Temperature, alloy condition and manufacturing route must be checked together.

standards.title: Selection of stainless steels and nickel alloys
standards.scope: ISO guidance for selection of stainless steels and nickel alloys for fasteners, linking material families and service conditions to corrosion and mechanical requirements.
standards.engineering_use: Useful during material selection before a specific product/property class is chosen. It should be read together with the applicable product and property standards.

standards.title: Stainless steel flat washers
standards.scope: ISO product/property standard for corrosion-resistant stainless-steel flat washers. It establishes washer designations and mechanical requirements for stainless washer applications.
standards.engineering_use: Use to select washers compatible with stainless bolt/nut systems, bearing loads and corrosion environment.

standards.title: Hexagon head bolts — product grades A and B
standards.scope: ISO product standard for hexagon head bolts with metric coarse threads and product grades A and B. It defines dimensional requirements for the product form and references the applicable mechanical property classes separately.
standards.engineering_use: Use for partially threaded metric hex-head bolts. Material/property class comes from standards such as ISO 898-1 or ISO 3506-1.

standards.title: Hexagon head screws — product grades A and B
standards.scope: ISO product standard for hexagon head screws with metric coarse threads and product grades A and B. It defines the product dimensions and full-thread configuration.
standards.engineering_use: Use for fully threaded metric hex-head screws; select mechanical property class independently.

standards.title: Hexagon regular nuts
standards.scope: ISO product standard for regular hexagon nuts with metric threads. It defines the nut geometry and dimensional series; mechanical performance is specified by the applicable nut property standard.
standards.engineering_use: Typically paired with ISO 4014/4017 and the corresponding ISO 898-2 or ISO 3506 nut class.

standards.title: Hexagon socket head cap screws
standards.scope: ISO product standard for hexagon socket head cap screws. It defines head, socket and dimensional requirements for this compact high-strength screw form.
standards.engineering_use: Common in machinery where a high-strength screw is needed with a compact head and internal hex drive. Property class must be specified separately.

standards.title: Plain washers — normal series
standards.scope: ISO product standard for plain washers, normal series. It defines washer dimensions and dimensional tolerances for metric fastener assemblies.
standards.engineering_use: Used to distribute bearing load and protect joint surfaces. Washer material, hardness and thickness must be checked for high-load applications.

standards.title: Metric screw threads — tolerances, principles and basic data
standards.scope: ISO framework for metric screw-thread tolerances, defining tolerance principles, basic concepts and the designation system used for thread tolerance classes.
standards.engineering_use: It is essential for interpreting designations such as 6H and 6g and for relating the basic thread geometry to manufacturing limits.

standards.title: Metric screw threads — limits of sizes
standards.scope: ISO standard specifying limits of size for metric screw-thread tolerance classes for internal and external threads.
standards.engineering_use: Used to determine whether a manufactured thread is within the permitted pitch-diameter and major/minor-diameter limits for the selected tolerance class.

standards.title: Metric screw threads — general plan
standards.scope: ISO general plan for ISO metric screw threads. It defines the preferred diameter/pitch combinations forming the general metric thread system.
standards.engineering_use: Use it to determine standard nominal diameter and pitch combinations before selecting a specific tolerance class.

standards.title: Selected sizes for metric threads
standards.scope: ISO table of selected metric screw-thread sizes and pitch combinations. It narrows the general metric thread plan to commonly selected nominal sizes.
standards.engineering_use: Useful for standard fastener selection and interchangeability; it is a size-selection reference rather than a mechanical-property standard.

standards.title: Electroplated coating systems
standards.scope: ISO standard for electroplated coating systems on threaded fasteners. It addresses coating-system designation, performance considerations and the relationship between coating and fastener application.
standards.engineering_use: Critical where corrosion protection, hydrogen-embrittlement risk, thread fit and friction/torque behaviour matter. The 2026 amendment should be considered when specifying current coating systems.

standards.title: Non-electrolytically applied zinc flake coating systems
standards.scope: ISO standard for non-electrolytically applied zinc-flake coating systems for fasteners. It covers coating-system requirements intended to provide corrosion protection without conventional electroplating.
standards.engineering_use: Particularly relevant to high-strength fasteners where hydrogen-embrittlement risk associated with electroplating must be controlled. Friction and top-coat characteristics affect assembly torque.

standards.title: Hot dip galvanized coatings
standards.scope: ISO standard for hot-dip galvanized coatings on threaded fasteners. It defines the coating process and dimensional/technical requirements associated with galvanized fastener systems.
standards.engineering_use: Used for robust atmospheric corrosion protection. Coating thickness can alter thread fit, so compatible bolt/nut systems and tapping/thread allowance must be considered.

standards.title: Torque/clamp force testing
standards.scope: ISO test standard for torque/clamp-force testing of threaded fasteners and joints. It provides a controlled method for evaluating the relationship between applied tightening torque and resulting clamp force.
standards.engineering_use: Useful for validating torque procedures, friction coefficients, coatings and lubrication. It is a test method, not a universal torque table.

standards.title: Fasteners — acceptance inspection
standards.scope: ISO acceptance-inspection standard for fasteners. It establishes general principles for sampling and inspection of fastener deliveries against specified requirements.
standards.engineering_use: Useful for incoming inspection and procurement quality control. Product-specific requirements and the purchase specification still govern the acceptance criteria.

standards.title: Alloy/stainless bolting for high-temperature or high-pressure service
standards.scope: ASTM specification for alloy-steel and stainless-steel bolting intended for high-temperature or high-pressure service and other special-purpose applications. It covers specified grades, heat treatment, mechanical requirements and testing for the products within its scope.
standards.engineering_use: Common in pressure equipment, valves, flanges and process piping. Grade selection must be matched to temperature, environment, product form and the applicable nut specification such as ASTM A194.

standards.title: Carbon/alloy/stainless nuts for high-pressure/high-temperature service
standards.scope: ASTM specification for carbon-steel, alloy-steel and stainless-steel nuts intended for high-pressure and/or high-temperature service. It defines grade-specific material and mechanical requirements.
standards.engineering_use: Frequently paired with ASTM A193 bolting. Nut grade, hardness, heat treatment and compatibility must be checked against the bolt grade and service conditions.

standards.title: Alloy/stainless bolting for low-temperature service
standards.scope: ASTM specification for alloy-steel and stainless-steel bolting intended for low-temperature service. It includes grade-specific mechanical and impact requirements where applicable.
standards.engineering_use: Commonly used for low-temperature pressure equipment and piping. Do not infer low-temperature suitability solely from a room-temperature tensile value.

standards.title: Carbon steel bolts and studs
standards.scope: ASTM specification covering carbon-steel bolts, studs and threaded rods in the general-purpose strength range. It establishes material, mechanical and dimensional-related requirements within the specified product scope.
standards.engineering_use: Used for general construction and mechanical fastening where high-strength or pressure-code bolting is not required.

standards.title: Structural bolts
standards.scope: ASTM structural-bolting specification covering high-strength structural bolts and associated grades/types for steel construction.
standards.engineering_use: Used in structural steel connections where bolt strength, geometry, installation and assembly requirements are governed by structural standards. Do not substitute pressure-equipment bolting without engineering review.

standards.title: Anchor bolts
standards.scope: ASTM specification for anchor bolts designed to anchor structural supports to concrete foundations. It defines several strength grades and identification requirements.
standards.engineering_use: Selection depends on structural load, embedment, geometry, weldability and installation system; the anchor bolt is part of the concrete/steel load path, not simply a generic bolt.

standards.title: Stainless steel bolts, screws and studs
standards.scope: ASTM specification for stainless-steel bolts, screws, studs and other externally threaded fasteners. It establishes alloy groups, conditions and mechanical requirements.
standards.engineering_use: Used for corrosion-resistant general-purpose and industrial fasteners. Verify alloy, condition, diameter-dependent strength and environmental suitability.

standards.title: Stainless steel nuts
standards.scope: ASTM specification for stainless-steel nuts. It establishes alloy groups and mechanical requirements for internally threaded fasteners.
standards.engineering_use: Typically paired with ASTM F593 stainless externally threaded fasteners; galling and material compatibility remain important considerations.

standards.title: Mechanical testing of threaded fasteners
standards.scope: ASTM test-method specification for determining mechanical and physical properties of externally and internally threaded fasteners. It covers methods such as tensile, proof-load, hardness and related testing.
standards.engineering_use: This is a testing standard rather than a grade specification; it tells the laboratory how to measure properties required by other fastener specifications.

standards.title: Square and hex bolts and screws — inch series
standards.scope: ASME dimensional standard for square and hex bolts, screws and lag screws in inch series. It defines product dimensions such as head geometry, widths across flats and lengths.
standards.engineering_use: Used to manufacture or identify inch-series fasteners. It does not establish the material grade or allowable design stress.

standards.title: Square and hex nuts — inch series
standards.scope: ASME dimensional standard for square and hex nuts in inch series. It defines nut dimensions and related dimensional requirements.
standards.engineering_use: Use with the applicable inch bolt/screw product and material specification; mechanical strength is defined separately.

standards.title: Pipe flanges and flanged fittings
standards.scope: ASME dimensional and pressure-rating standard for pipe flanges and flanged fittings, including pressure-temperature ratings, dimensions, materials, tolerances, marking and testing requirements.
standards.engineering_use: It is central to flange joint design in process piping. Bolt selection must be coordinated with flange rating, gasket, temperature, material group and the governing piping/pressure code.

standards.title: Valves — flanged, threaded and welding end
standards.scope: ASME standard for valves with flanged, threaded and welding ends. It addresses pressure-temperature ratings, materials, dimensions, design, testing and other valve requirements.
standards.engineering_use: Fasteners used in valves must be selected consistently with the valve design, pressure-temperature service and applicable material specifications.

standards.title: Mechanical and material requirements for mechanical fasteners
standards.scope: SAE specification establishing mechanical and material requirements for inch-series mechanical fasteners, including strength grades and associated tests.
standards.engineering_use: Common reference for automotive and general machinery fasteners. Grade numbers such as Grade 5 and Grade 8 describe mechanical requirements, not a universal material chemistry.

standards.title: Alloy and carbon steel bolting for oil and gas
standards.scope: API specification for alloy and carbon-steel bolting used in the oil and natural-gas industry. It establishes quality, manufacturing, inspection and traceability requirements beyond simply naming a material grade.
standards.engineering_use: Useful where oil-and-gas procurement requires controlled bolting production, qualification and documentation.

standards.title: Corrosion-resistant bolting for oil and gas
standards.scope: API specification for corrosion-resistant bolting used in oil and natural-gas applications. It establishes material, manufacturing, inspection and quality requirements for corrosion-resistant fasteners.
standards.engineering_use: Relevant to demanding oil-and-gas service where corrosion resistance and traceability are critical; material selection remains service-specific.

standards.title: Materials for H2S-containing oil and gas environments
standards.scope: International standard for selection and qualification of metallic materials for equipment used in H2S-containing oil and gas production environments. It addresses sulfide stress cracking and related cracking mechanisms through material, hardness, heat treatment, environment and service restrictions.
standards.engineering_use: It is not a simple list of “sour-service grades.” Compliance depends on the material, product form, condition and actual environment. Use the applicable part and environmental limits.

standards.title: High-strength structural bolting assemblies for preloading
standards.scope: European standard series for high-strength structural bolting assemblies suitable for preloaded structural joints. It defines system-specific bolt/nut/washer assemblies and performance requirements.
standards.engineering_use: Used in structural steelwork where controlled preload is required. Assembly components should be treated as a matched system, not mixed arbitrarily.

standards.title: Non-preloaded structural bolting assemblies
standards.scope: European standard for non-preloaded structural bolting assemblies. It specifies requirements for assemblies intended for structural joints where preloading is not the governing installation principle.
standards.engineering_use: Useful for structural steel connections where the joint design does not require controlled preloaded assembly.

standards.title: Hexagon bolts
standards.scope: Japanese Industrial Standard for hexagon bolts, defining product dimensions and related requirements for the Japanese metric fastener system.
standards.engineering_use: Used for Japanese equipment and drawings; verify the exact JIS edition, thread/tolerance and mechanical property specification before substitution with ISO products.

standards.title: Hexagon nuts
standards.scope: Japanese Industrial Standard for hexagon nuts, defining product dimensions and related requirements for Japanese metric fastener systems.
standards.engineering_use: Use with the corresponding JIS bolt and nut property requirements; dimensional similarity to ISO does not automatically prove interchangeability.

standards.title: Hexagon head bolts, full thread
standards.scope: Chinese national standard for hexagon head bolts with full thread. It defines the product geometry and dimensions for the specified Chinese metric fastener family.
standards.engineering_use: Common in Chinese equipment and procurement. Confirm grade, tolerance, material and the exact GB/T edition when translating to ISO/DIN equivalents.

standards.title: Hexagon nuts
standards.scope: Chinese national standard for hexagon nuts. It defines the product dimensions and applicable nut forms in the Chinese metric system.
standards.engineering_use: Use with the corresponding Chinese bolt/property specification and verify equivalence rather than relying only on nominal thread size.

standards.title: Thin hexagon nuts (chamfered)
standards.scope: Thin hexagon nuts, commonly used where axial space is limited; dimensional/product reference.
standards.engineering_use: Select the nut together with the bolt/property class and verify engagement and prevailing-load requirements.

standards.title: Thin hexagon nuts (un-chamfered)
standards.scope: Thin un-chamfered hexagon nuts for metric fastening applications.
standards.engineering_use: Useful for space-constrained assemblies; verify thread, strength and mating-bolt requirements.

standards.title: Prevailing torque type all-metal hexagon nuts
standards.scope: Metric all-metal prevailing-torque hexagon nuts for applications requiring resistance to loosening.
standards.engineering_use: Defines product/dimensional requirements; verify prevailing torque and temperature suitability for the exact type.

standards.title: Prevailing torque type all-metal hexagon nuts, high type
standards.scope: High all-metal prevailing-torque hexagon nuts for metric fastening.
standards.engineering_use: Used where a reusable/non-polymer locking feature is needed; verify temperature and prevailing-torque requirements.

standards.title: Prevailing torque type steel nuts
standards.scope: Functional requirements and test methods for prevailing-torque type steel nuts.
standards.engineering_use: Use for qualification/control of prevailing torque rather than as a substitute for the dimensional product standard.

standards.title: Plain washers with chamfer — normal series
standards.scope: Dimensions for chamfered metric plain washers.
standards.engineering_use: Use where the chamfered washer geometry is required by the assembly drawing.

standards.title: Plain washers — large series
standards.scope: Large-series metric plain washers with increased outside diameter.
standards.engineering_use: Useful for lower bearing stress on softer materials and oversized holes; verify bearing design.

standards.title: Plain washers — extra-large series
standards.scope: Extra-large-series metric plain washers.
standards.engineering_use: Used where very large bearing area is required; confirm structural bearing and clearance conditions.

standards.title: Countersunk head hexagon socket screws
standards.scope: Dimensional/product requirements for metric countersunk hexagon socket screws.
standards.engineering_use: For flush-head assemblies; verify countersink geometry and property class with the applicable mechanical specification.

standards.title: Hexalobular socket pan head screws
standards.scope: Metric pan-head screws with internal hexalobular drive.
standards.engineering_use: Product geometry and drive interface reference; mechanical class and material are specified separately.

standards.title: Hexagon socket head shoulder screws
standards.scope: Dimensional requirements for metric shoulder screws with hexagon socket.
standards.engineering_use: Used for pivots, locating and controlled-clearance applications; verify shoulder diameter/length and material.

standards.title: Hexagon socket head cap screws with low head
standards.scope: Low-head metric socket screws for reduced head height.
standards.engineering_use: Useful where conventional socket-head clearance is unavailable; verify reduced head capacity and grade.

standards.title: Tolerances for fasteners — Part 1
standards.scope: General dimensional and geometrical tolerances for bolts, screws, studs and nuts.
standards.engineering_use: Use with the applicable product standard when checking dimensional acceptance and interchangeability.

standards.title: Carbon and alloy steel nuts
standards.scope: Specification for carbon and alloy steel nuts for general and pressure-related fastening applications.
standards.engineering_use: Common US nut material/property specification; select grade and size range to match the bolt and service.

standards.title: Hardened steel washers
standards.scope: Specification for hardened steel washers used with structural and high-strength fasteners.
standards.engineering_use: Provides washer material/hardness and dimensions by type; use the structural fastener system requirements as applicable.

standards.title: Nonferrous nuts for general use
standards.scope: Specification for nonferrous nuts for general applications.
standards.engineering_use: Covers selected copper-, aluminum- and nickel-alloy nut materials; verify corrosion, strength and galling compatibility.

standards.title: Nonferrous bolts, hex cap screws and studs
standards.scope: Specification for nonferrous bolts, screws and studs.
standards.engineering_use: Provides material/property requirements for selected nonferrous fasteners; confirm product dimensions separately.

standards.title: Surface discontinuities of bolts, screws and studs
standards.scope: Requirements for surface discontinuities in bolts, screws and studs.
standards.engineering_use: Useful for quality inspection and acceptance of production fasteners.

standards.title: Surface discontinuities of nuts
standards.scope: Requirements for surface discontinuities in nuts.
standards.engineering_use: Supports inspection of cracks, seams and other discontinuities in nuts.

standards.title: Socket cap, shoulder, set screws and related products
standards.scope: Dimensional requirements for socket-type cap screws, shoulder screws, set screws and related inch fasteners.
standards.engineering_use: Primary dimensional reference for many internal-drive inch fasteners.

standards.title: Machine screws, tapping screws and metallic drive screws
standards.scope: Dimensional and product requirements for inch machine screws, tapping screws and related drive screws.
standards.engineering_use: Used for general-purpose small fastening hardware; verify material and strength requirements separately.

standards.title: Prevailing torque type nuts
standards.scope: Functional and dimensional requirements for selected inch prevailing-torque nuts.
standards.engineering_use: Use for locking-nut selection and inspection; verify temperature and reuse limitations.

standards.title: Washers — square and round
standards.scope: Dimensional requirements for inch plain and related washers.
standards.engineering_use: Provides washer dimensions for general inch fastening assemblies.

standards.title: Plain washers
standards.scope: Dimensional requirements for inch plain washers.
standards.engineering_use: Select washer series based on bolt size and bearing requirements.

standards.title: Mechanical and material requirements for steel nuts
standards.scope: Mechanical and material requirements for inch-series steel nuts.
standards.engineering_use: Provides nut grade requirements used with SAE/ASME bolting systems.

standards.title: Prevailing torque nuts
standards.scope: Requirements and test methods for prevailing-torque type nuts.
standards.engineering_use: Used to control locking performance of prevailing-torque nuts.

standards.title: Wellhead and Christmas tree equipment
standards.scope: Requirements for wellhead and Christmas-tree equipment, including pressure-containing/controlling components and associated bolting requirements.
standards.engineering_use: Relevant to upstream pressure equipment; bolting selection must follow the complete equipment specification and PSL/temperature class.

standards.title: Subsea wellhead and tree equipment
standards.scope: Requirements for subsea wellhead and tree equipment.
standards.engineering_use: Relevant to subsea equipment qualification and bolting; environment, material and service requirements are project-specific.

standards.title: Temperature effects on bolted flanged joints
standards.scope: Guidance for evaluating temperature effects on bolted flanged joints.
standards.engineering_use: Useful when thermal transients can change preload, leakage performance or joint loads.

standards.title: High-strength structural bolting assemblies — Part 1
standards.scope: General requirements for high-strength structural bolting assemblies for preloading.
standards.engineering_use: Use as part of EN 14399 system selection; assembly configuration, tightening method and conformity are critical.

standards.title: High-strength structural bolting assemblies — suitability for preloading
standards.scope: Suitability-for-preloading requirements for high-strength structural bolting assemblies.
standards.engineering_use: Defines system-level requirements rather than a generic bolt-only strength class.

standards.title: Non-preloaded structural bolting assemblies — Part 1
standards.scope: Requirements for non-preloaded structural bolting assemblies.
standards.engineering_use: For structural joints where controlled preloading is not specified; verify assembly and execution requirements.

materials.note: Typical specification minimums vary by diameter/product condition; use exact edition tables.
materials.description: Chromium-molybdenum alloy-steel pressure bolting grade widely used for flanges, valves and pressure equipment. It is selected for strength and elevated-temperature capability, but design allowables and temperature limits must come from the governing code and exact material tables.
materials.temperature_note: Broad material-family screening range only; verify exact grade, product condition, diameter, edition and code-specific temperature limits before design.

materials.note: Hardness and sour-service requirements must be checked against the governing specification.
materials.description: Modified B7-type Cr-Mo bolting with controlled hardness and strength intended for applications where sour-service restrictions may apply. NACE/ISO 15156 qualification depends on the complete material condition and environment, not the grade name alone.
materials.temperature_note: Broad material-family screening range only; verify exact grade, product condition, diameter, edition and code-specific temperature limits before design.

materials.note: Use exact diameter/temperature tables for design.

coatings.name: Electroplated zinc
coatings.risk: Hydrogen embrittlement risk for susceptible high-strength steels; process controls required.
coatings.procedure: Typical sequence: alkaline cleaning/degreasing → rinsing → acid activation/pickling as appropriate → zinc electrodeposition → rinsing → conversion treatment/sealant/topcoat when specified → controlled drying → dimensional, appearance, adhesion and corrosion/process verification. For susceptible high-strength steel, hydrogen-embrittlement controls must be part of the qualified process; post-plating baking is not a universal substitute for process control.
coatings.engineering: Common for general corrosion protection. Coating thickness, supplementary treatment and lubricant affect corrosion life, thread fit and torque–tension behavior. For high-strength fasteners, specify the complete coating system and hydrogen-control requirements rather than simply “zinc plated.”
references: ASTM F1940 — Hydrogen embrittlement process control

coatings.name: Hot-dip galvanizing
coatings.risk: Thread allowance, coating thickness and fit must be checked.
coatings.procedure: Typical fastener sequence: surface preparation/cleaning → fluxing or equivalent pretreatment → immersion in molten zinc → withdrawal/drainage → controlled cooling/quenching where specified → inspection of coating, thread fit and appearance. Fastener geometry and thread allowance are designed around the coating system; nuts and bolts should be specified as a matched galvanized system.
coatings.engineering: Produces a relatively thick zinc coating with sacrificial/cathodic protection and is widely used outdoors and in structural applications. Thread dimensional changes and friction scatter are important for assembly preload. Current ISO 10684:2004 remains published while a replacement edition is under development.

coatings.name: Zinc flake
coatings.procedure: Typical sequence: clean/degrease → controlled surface preparation → apply zinc-flake base coat by dip-spin, spray or approved process → cure/bake according to the qualified coating system → apply optional topcoat/lubricant → cure → verify thickness, appearance, adhesion and friction where required. The process is non-electrolytic, so the hydrogen-introduction mechanism differs from conventional electroplating.
coatings.engineering: Especially useful for high-strength fasteners where corrosion performance and low risk of process-induced internal hydrogen embrittlement are important. Friction is a property of the complete coating/topcoat/lubricant system, not the zinc-flake name alone.
references: ASTM F1940 — Process control for IHE

coatings.name: Phosphate
coatings.procedure: Typical sequence: clean/degrease → rinse → activate/pickle when required → phosphate conversion treatment → rinse or post-treatment → dry → apply oil, wax, sealant or paint when specified. Manganese phosphate is commonly selected where wear-in and lubricity are important; zinc phosphate is frequently used as a paint/lubricant base.
coatings.engineering: Phosphate is a conversion coating rather than a thick metallic barrier coating. Its corrosion and friction performance depends strongly on the phosphate type, crystal structure, oil/sealant and assembly lubricant. Specify the complete treatment and post-treatment.

coatings.name: Black oxide
coatings.procedure: Typical sequence: clean/degrease → alkaline black-oxide treatment appropriate to the substrate → rinse → post-treatment/seal or oil → dry. Black oxide is intentionally thin, so dimensional change is small compared with galvanizing. The oil/sealant is normally a major part of the corrosion-performance system.
coatings.engineering: Useful where appearance, low dimensional build and mild corrosion protection are required. Bare black oxide should not be treated as a heavy-duty corrosion barrier; specify the post-treatment and service environment.

coatings.name: PTFE / fluoropolymer
coatings.procedure: Typical sequence: degrease/clean → substrate preparation or blast/chemical preparation as required → apply primer where the qualified system requires it → apply fluoropolymer layer(s) by spray, dip or other approved method → flash/dry → bake/cure → inspect coating thickness, continuity and friction. The exact cure window is manufacturer/system specific.
coatings.engineering: Selected for low friction, chemical resistance and controlled torque. Because friction can be much lower than for uncoated steel, the same tightening torque can generate substantially higher preload. Use coating-specific torque–tension data.

coatings.name: Stainless passivation
coatings.risk: Not a plating; process affects surface condition.
coatings.procedure: Typical sequence: remove oil and fabrication contamination → mechanically or chemically descale/pickle when necessary → rinse thoroughly → apply qualified nitric, citric or electrochemical passivation treatment → rinse/neutralize as required → dry without recontamination → verify cleanliness/passivation by the specified acceptance test. Passivation is not a substitute for removing heavy oxide scale or weld heat tint when those remain.
coatings.engineering: Passivation restores a clean stainless surface and supports formation of the passive chromium-rich oxide film. It does not add a plated corrosion barrier and does not change the base alloy into a higher corrosion-resistance grade.
references: ASTM A380/A380M — Cleaning, descaling and passivation

coatings.name: Zinc-flake coating
coatings.risk: Hydrogen embrittlement risk is generally lower than electroplating, but process, topcoat and friction control still require verification.
coatings.procedure: Same basic process family as zinc flake: controlled cleaning → substrate preparation → non-electrolytic zinc-flake base application → cure → optional topcoat/lubricant → final cure and inspection. Process parameters must be qualified for the specific coating chemistry, fastener geometry and required friction class.
coatings.engineering: Use when corrosion resistance, dimensional control and reduced hydrogen risk for high-strength steel are priorities. The topcoat/lubricant can materially change friction and chemical resistance.

coatings.name: Hot-dip galvanized zinc
coatings.risk: Thread dimensional changes, friction variation and hydrogen-related concerns must be assessed for the specific product/process.
coatings.procedure: Prepare the steel surface, apply flux/pretreatment, immerse in molten zinc, withdraw and drain, cool/finish and inspect. For threaded fasteners, coating build and thread allowance must be compatible with the mating nut and the specified assembly method.
coatings.engineering: A heavy sacrificial zinc coating suited to atmospheric exposure. Coating thickness and roughness influence thread fit and torque–tension scatter, so galvanized fasteners should be specified and assembled as a controlled system.

coatings.name: Geomet / zinc-flake system
coatings.risk: Do not assume friction coefficient from coating name alone; use tested assembly data.
coatings.procedure: Treat this as a proprietary zinc-flake coating system: clean and prepare the substrate → apply qualified basecoat → cure → apply system-specific topcoat/lubricant → cure → verify coating thickness, appearance, adhesion, corrosion performance and friction. Do not infer process temperatures or friction values from the trade name alone.
coatings.engineering: Useful for high-performance corrosion protection and controlled assembly friction. Procurement documents should identify the exact product/system, coating class and friction requirements rather than only the trade family.

coatings.name: PTFE topcoat
coatings.risk: Low friction can greatly increase preload for a given torque; verify torque-tension data.
coatings.procedure: Typical sequence: clean/prepare substrate → apply primer where required → spray/dip PTFE-containing topcoat → flash/dry → controlled thermal cure → inspect thickness and continuity → determine torque–tension/friction for the finished fastener system. Cure temperature must be compatible with both coating and fastener metallurgy.
coatings.engineering: Low friction is the key engineering variable. Torque-based tightening can over-preload a PTFE-coated fastener if uncoated torque values are reused. Use measured or qualified torque–tension data and specify the friction range.

coatings.name: Xylan-type fluoropolymer coating
coatings.risk: Coating thickness, temperature capability and friction coefficient must be controlled.
coatings.procedure: Typical proprietary-system process: degrease/clean → blast or otherwise prepare the substrate → primer application when specified → fluoropolymer topcoat application → flash/dry → controlled bake/cure → inspect thickness, adhesion, continuity and friction. The exact chemistry and cure schedule must come from the coating supplier specification.
coatings.engineering: Can combine corrosion resistance with low and relatively controlled friction. Coating thickness, temperature capability and friction must be treated as controlled design inputs, particularly for pressure-boundary and high-preload joints.

coatings.name: Phosphate coating
coatings.risk: Performance depends strongly on oil or sealant; verify friction and corrosion requirements.
coatings.procedure: Typical process: alkaline cleaning → rinse → activation/pickling as needed → phosphate conversion → rinse/post-treatment → dry → oil, sealant or paint. The post-treatment is normally essential when corrosion protection is required.
coatings.engineering: Phosphate improves surface characteristics and can provide useful lubricity, but it is not normally a stand-alone heavy corrosion barrier. Friction is strongly affected by oil and assembly lubricant.

coatings.name: Cadmium coating
coatings.use: corrosion protection and lubricity in selected aerospace uses
coatings.risk: Environmental restrictions and health controls apply; do not substitute without specification approval.
coatings.procedure: Typical controlled electroplating sequence: clean/degrease → activate/pickle → cadmium electrodeposition → rinse → conversion treatment/seal where specified → controlled drying and inspection. For high-strength steels, hydrogen-control and post-plating treatment requirements must be explicitly qualified. Cadmium processing requires strict environmental and occupational controls.
coatings.engineering: Historically important in aerospace because of corrosion protection, lubricity and compatibility characteristics. Modern environmental restrictions mean cadmium should only be selected where the governing specification and regulatory controls explicitly permit it.

coatings.name: Silver plating
coatings.risk: Friction and compatibility depend on mating materials and service temperature.
coatings.procedure: Typical sequence: clean/activate substrate → apply appropriate underplate when required → electrodeposit silver to the specified thickness → rinse → optional anti-tarnish/post-treatment → inspect thickness, adhesion and surface condition. Aerospace or electrical applications normally require a qualified supplier process specification.
coatings.engineering: Silver can provide low friction and anti-galling behavior in selected applications and retains useful properties at elevated temperature. Compatibility, tarnishing, galvanic effects and friction should be evaluated for the actual mating materials.

coatings.name: Nickel plating
coatings.risk: Hardness, adhesion, hydrogen effects and friction must be verified for high-strength fasteners.
coatings.procedure: Typical sequence: clean/degrease → activate substrate → optional strike/underplate → nickel electrodeposition → rinse → post-treatment if specified → inspect thickness, adhesion and hardness. Electroless nickel uses a different deposition chemistry and should not be assumed equivalent to electrolytic nickel.
coatings.engineering: Provides a hard, dimensionally controllable corrosion-resistant surface. For high-strength steel fasteners, hydrogen uptake, coating adhesion, internal stress and friction need process-specific verification.

warnings.text: Do not infer NACE/ISO 15156 compliance from a grade name alone. Check material, hardness, heat treatment, product form and environment.
warnings.description: Sour-service selection is controlled by H2S partial pressure, pH, chloride level, temperature, stress state and the material/product condition. A nominal grade such as B7M or a stainless designation is not sufficient evidence of compliance.
warnings.recommended_check: Verify the applicable NACE MR0175/ISO 15156 part, material family, hardness limits, heat treatment, product form and environmental limits.

warnings.text: A bolt grade is not an allowable stress. Use the governing pressure code and exact material tables.
warnings.description: Pressure-equipment bolting is part of a pressure-boundary joint and must be selected using the governing construction code, flange/valve standard, temperature and material tables. Tensile strength is not the same as allowable stress.
warnings.recommended_check: Check the code allowable stress, bolt-load basis, flange/gasket requirements, temperature derating and assembly procedure.

warnings.text: High-strength hardened steels plus some electroplating processes require specific controls.
warnings.description: High-strength steels can be susceptible to hydrogen-assisted cracking, particularly after certain surface treatments or in hydrogen-generating environments. Electroplating and cleaning processes can introduce hydrogen.
warnings.recommended_check: Control coating selection, baking/process qualification where required, hardness/strength level and service environment; verify the applicable coating standard.

warnings.text: Austenitic stainless and nickel-alloy threads can gall; lubrication, surface condition, speed and preload procedure matter.
warnings.description: Galling is adhesive surface damage that can occur during tightening, especially with austenitic stainless and nickel-alloy threads. High contact pressure, poor lubrication, surface roughness and repeated assembly increase risk.
warnings.recommended_check: Use compatible materials, controlled lubrication/coating, appropriate tightening speed and a validated assembly procedure.

warnings.text: Room-temperature strength must not be used as a high-temperature allowable stress.
warnings.description: Fastener strength, preload retention, creep/relaxation and material compatibility can change substantially with temperature. Room-temperature tensile strength is not a valid substitute for a temperature-specific allowable.
warnings.recommended_check: Use temperature-dependent material/code data and assess thermal expansion mismatch, relaxation and joint preload at operating temperature.

warnings.text: Bolt fatigue is a joint problem: preload, stiffness, external-load fraction and stress concentration matter.
warnings.description: Fastener fatigue is governed by the joint, not simply by the bolt ultimate strength. Preload, joint stiffness, external load fraction, stress concentration, surface condition and load spectrum all influence fatigue life.
warnings.recommended_check: Perform a joint-level fatigue assessment for cyclic service and avoid relying on static tensile capacity alone.

warnings.text: K in T=KFd is system-specific and changes with friction, coating, lubrication and assembly method.
warnings.description: The nut factor K is an empirical representation of friction and is strongly affected by thread and bearing friction, coating, lubrication, surface finish and assembly speed. A generic K value can produce large preload errors.
warnings.recommended_check: Use validated friction data or torque-tension testing when preload is critical; ISO 16047 provides a framework for torque/clamp-force testing.

warnings.text: Tensile bolt capacity does not prove internal/external thread engagement capacity.
warnings.description: A bolt can have adequate tensile capacity while the internal thread, external thread or tapped component strips first. Engagement length, material strength, thread geometry and load distribution determine thread capacity.
warnings.recommended_check: Check thread shear/stripping capacity, engagement length and the weakest threaded component, especially for soft materials and short engagement.

warnings.text: Dissimilar metals in wet conductive environments can form galvanic couples.
warnings.description: When dissimilar conductive metals are exposed to an electrolyte, the more anodic material can corrode preferentially. Fastener/joint geometry and coating damage can concentrate the effect.
warnings.recommended_check: Assess the galvanic series, electrolyte exposure, area ratio and coating strategy; isolate dissimilar metals where appropriate.

warnings.text: Legacy DIN numbers remain common on drawings and installed equipment; substitution needs engineering/document control.
warnings.description: Many DIN numbers remain on old drawings, equipment and spare-parts lists even after corresponding DIN EN ISO standards were adopted. Similar dimensions do not guarantee identical tolerances, grades, head dimensions or inspection requirements.
warnings.recommended_check: Treat substitution as an engineering/document-control decision and verify the exact old and new standards before changing procurement.

warnings.text: Initial preload can fall after tightening because of surface roughness, coatings, gasket compression and local yielding.
warnings.description: Account for joint settling where preload retention is critical.
warnings.recommended_check: Use joint-specific preload verification or test data; inspect contact surfaces and gasket behavior.

warnings.text: A washer can prevent local indentation or punching only if its geometry and hardness are adequate for the joint materials.
warnings.description: Check bearing pressure under the head/nut and the supporting material.
warnings.recommended_check: Calculate bearing stress and verify washer dimensions/hardness against the applicable standard.

warnings.text: External tensile loads can unload the bolt and cause separation even when nominal preload is high.
warnings.description: Evaluate bolt load versus joint compression using joint stiffness and load-introduction assumptions.
warnings.recommended_check: Perform a joint separation/slip assessment for critical connections.

warnings.text: Insufficient engagement can cause internal thread stripping before bolt tensile capacity is reached.
warnings.description: Verify engagement length, internal thread material and thread quality.
warnings.recommended_check: Check stripping capacity using the governing design method and actual thread dimensions.

warnings.text: A large fraction of tightening torque can be consumed at the bearing surface rather than producing bolt tension.
warnings.description: Coating, lubrication and washer condition strongly affect torque-tension behavior.
warnings.recommended_check: Use a validated torque coefficient or tension-control method.

warnings.text: High-strength steel exposed to hydrogen-generating processes can suffer delayed brittle cracking.
warnings.description: Electroplating and acidic cleaning are common process sources.
warnings.recommended_check: Specify the applicable hydrogen-embrittlement control, baking and inspection requirements.

warnings.text: Different thermal expansion of bolt and joint materials changes preload during heating and cooling.
warnings.description: This is important in engines, pressure equipment, cryogenic systems and hot piping.
warnings.recommended_check: Calculate thermally induced preload changes using actual materials and joint geometry.

warnings.text: Pressure and external moments can rotate a flange and redistribute bolt loads.
warnings.description: A bolt stress check alone may not predict leakage or local flange behavior.
warnings.recommended_check: Use the applicable flange/joint calculation method and evaluate rotation and gasket seating.

warnings.text: Misalignment, prying and eccentric load paths can impose bending in addition to axial tension.
warnings.description: Combined loading can reduce fatigue margin and effective preload.
warnings.recommended_check: Evaluate combined tension, shear and bending where load path is eccentric.

warnings.text: Damaged or misaligned threads can produce false torque readings and inadequate engagement.
warnings.description: Particularly important in stainless and fine-thread assemblies.
warnings.recommended_check: Inspect thread condition, alignment and starting torque before final tightening.
